Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap gives smooth, tear-free gameplay at a balanced TDP. FSR at 1024x640 recovers visual clarity while keeping the GPU from being overwhelmed in busy zoo areas.

profiles.Summary: Planet Zoo is a demanding simulation title whose recommended specs (GTX 1070) comfortably exceed what the Steam Deck GPU can offer, so expect low-to-medium settings and FSR to be necessary for a playable experience, especially in large, populated zoos. The game runs under Proton with a gold ProtonDB rating, meaning most players get it working well with minor tweaks.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended requirements versus Deck GPU capability. On your first session, check frame rate in a busy zoo area with many animals and guests — that is the worst-case scenario, and you may need to drop to Max Battery settings if the Optimal profile stutters.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a low TDP keeps the battery alive for extended sessions. Performance will drop in heavily populated or large zoos — reduce Crowd Detail further if needed.

KnownIssues: Performance degrades significantly as zoo population and guest count grow — frame drops are common in late-game saves
No native controller/gamepad UI; mouse and keyboard via touchscreen or trackpads is recommended for menu navigation
The game may require Proton compatibility layer tuning; some users report minor shader compilation stutters on first launch
HDR output may not function correctly under Proton on SteamOS

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full TDP and max GPU clock push the Deck as hard as it can go; expect the 50 fps cap to hold in early/small zoos but drop toward 40 in large, late-game saves. Battery life will be short at this setting.

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh / 40 fps cap is the sweet spot for this style of simulation game on OLED — buttery-smooth for panning around habitats with a reasonable battery cost; Animal Detail is prioritised high since animals are the centrepiece of the game.

profiles.Summary: Planet Zoo is a demanding simulation title that runs on Deck via Proton at gold tier, meaning it generally works but may require some tweaking; the RDNA 2 GPU sits below the recommended spec so expect lower settings and FSR to be necessary, especially in complex, populated zoos. Performance can vary significantly with zoo size and animal count, so frame rates quoted here are for a moderately developed zoo rather than a bare starting area.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements versus Deck GPU class (roughly GTX 1050 Ti) and the general behaviour of Frontier's simulation engine. On your first run, check fps in a mid-development zoo and note how performance changes as the park grows — drop to the Optimal or Max Battery profile if the frame rate becomes unstable.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and an 8 W TDP cap keeps the APU cool and the battery lasting through long sessions; animal and texture quality are kept slightly higher than the rest since those matter most visually in a zoo sim.

KnownIssues: Performance degrades noticeably as zoo complexity, animal count, and guest numbers increase — frame rates quoted assume a mid-sized zoo, not a maxed-out late-game park.
No native Linux build; runs through Proton and is rated Playable (not Verified), so minor UI or input quirks may appear.
The game's UI and menus are designed for mouse and keyboard; controller navigation works but can feel cumbersome for fine habitat placement.
Some ProtonDB reporters note occasional stutters when loading new zoo areas or autosaving.

MaxPerformance.Notes: This profile pushes the Deck to its limit and will hold near-60 fps in a small or early-game zoo, but expect dips into the 40s in a large, crowded park — if that happens, drop Crowd Detail and Foliage Quality to Low first.
